correctness.rationale: The number of distinct adjacent-two-deletion descendants is 1+∑_{i=1}^{n−2}1_{x_i≠x_{i+2}}, because outputs y_i=y_j imply period two of the intervening source substring and equal-output blocks are contiguous. The binary difference map δ_i=x_i⊕x_{i+1}, δ_n=x_n is invertible, and the last bit selects a unique lift from syndrome modulo n to modulo 2n. The weighted transition enumerator F_n(q,z) is expressed through the 2×2 transfer product J D_i(q). For a root q of order d|n/2, d even, nonconstant cyclic rotation orbits cancel and constant orbits give tr P_d=0; det P_d=−(1−z²)^d implies P_d²=(1−z²)^d I and F_n(q,z)=2K. For primitive order n, reversal/complement pairs contributions with opposite q^{n/2} signs, giving F_n(q,z)=0. q=1 gives F_n=2G. Fourier inversion yields the claimed four-exceptional versus remaining 2n−4 syndrome classes. Independent exact enumeration of all words n=4,8,16 and separate DP at n=32 matched every coefficient, covering examples but not replacing the all-powers-of-two Fourier proof.

value.rationale: The precise number of distinct outputs per codeword is a canonical invariant of the perfect two-burst deletion code, relevant to variable sphere geometry and decoding/covering heterogeneity. It refines the recently established global count into a full sharp two-class syndrome-conditional distribution for every power of two, not an arbitrary finite recomputation.

final_claim: For n=2^r≥4, the number of distinct adjacent-two-deletion outputs per word in each binary differential VT class has only two exact enumerator polynomials: [2G+(n−2)K]/n for four syndrome classes and [2G−2K]/n for the others, G=z(1+z)^(n−2), K=z(1−z)^(n/2)(1+z)^(n/2−2).
limitations: No extension beyond n powers of two or to non-binary alphabets and no performance claim.
Four exceptional syndrome classes comprise a≡0 or n/2 modulo n, not a different code convention.
